# Weekly Book Topics 50Q - week of 27 Sep 2026 (Mon 28 Sep - Sat 3 Oct)

*Auto-generated for UPSC CSE 2027 prep. Feeds the website's Sectional practice flow. Static book-topic set, not current affairs.*

## Week focus

**Basis:** the **Sunday Sweep dated 2026-09-27**, which plans **Sun 27 Sep -> Sat 3 Oct 2026** - the upcoming week after this Sunday run, closing **F9** in Phase 1B. Sunday is revision-only, so all new reading falls in **Mon 28 Sep - Sat 3 Oct**, and this set tests those six days. The Sweep's resource calendar asks for the Book-topics 50Q to be run **cold against Monday's Laxmikanth block** as a pre-read diagnostic, so Polity is the anchor.

| Block | Reading (per Sweep) | Qs | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Polity - Other Constitutional Dimensions** | Laxmikanth: Official Language, Public Services, Rights & Liabilities of Govt, Special Provisions for Certain Classes, Co-operative Societies (Mon) | Q1-14 | The week's named pre-read target and the last of Laxmikanth's constitutional text. Arts 343-351, the Eighth Schedule batches, 309-312, 299-300, 334/338B/340, Part IXB and *Rajendra N. Shah*. **Tribunals is deliberately left out** - Arts 323A/323B and *L. Chandra Kumar* were tested on 30 Aug. |
| **Economy - Survey social sector** | Economic Survey Vol I social-sector + thematic chapters (Tue) | Q15-21 | Tests the measurement apparatus you need to read those chapters - HDI, MPI, poverty lines, GER/NER, PLFS, Gini - not any edition-specific figure. Economy is studied from **NCERT + Vivek Singh, not Mrunal**. |
| **Medieval History - Arabs, Turks, Delhi Sultanate** | TN Class 11, 712-1526 (Wed) | Q22-33 | First appearance of the Sultanate in any book-topics set; the Sweep flags it as the thinnest block. Institutions over dates. |
| **Sci-Tech - Defence + Nuclear** | Vision IAS Sci-Tech (Thu) | Q34-37 | **Declared revision round.** Missiles, doctrine and the three-stage programme were tested on 09 and 11 Aug, so this set is cut to four questions and restricted to angles not asked then: export-control regimes, the PFBR, hypersonics, ITER. |
| **IR - Russia + Eurasia** | Treaty spine -> defence -> energy -> connectivity -> Central Asia (Fri) | Q38-43 | Russia had one question on 30 Aug (the agreement ladder); that is not repeated. The weight is on connectivity (INSTC, Ashgabat, Chabahar) and Central Asia, which are new. |
| **Geography - NCERT-12 Ch 9-10** | Planning & Sustainable Development; Transport & Communication (Sat) | Q44-50 | Clean advance from Ch 7-8 (13 Sep). Target-area programmes, Bharmaur, the Indira Gandhi Canal, corridors, waterways, pipelines, Konkan. |

**Repeat check.** The last six-plus book-topics sets (16 Aug - 20 Sep) closed Laxmikanth through the non-constitutional bodies, Vivek Singh through Ch 14 and the Survey's macro/real-sector half, Ancient through the Cholas, Shankar's legislation chapter, Art & Culture temples/caves, Geography NCERT-12 Ch 1-8 and IR US/China/Russia(1 Q)/neighbourhood/Pakistan. Only Sci-Tech is a revisit, and it is declared and minimised above. No item is claimed as an exact UPSC PYQ; stems are PYQ-pattern-inspired. The PFBR criticality date (6 April 2026, DAE) and India's Ashgabat accession (3 Feb 2018) were web-verified.

## How to use

**Sunday evening, 60 minutes, timed, no notes** - after the 60-Q sectional, not instead of it. Q1-14 are meant to be attempted **cold**: mark every Polity item sure / 50:50 / guessed, and let Monday's reading answer the 50:50s. Q15-50 test reading you have not yet done either, so treat the whole score as a baseline, then **re-take blind on Saturday 3 Oct** once the week is closed; the gap is the honest measure of the week.

Debrief only wrong answers and lucky guesses, one line each on *why the wrong statement is wrong*. The traps this week are mostly **inversions** (Devanagari vs international numerals; nominated vs elected; one-third vs half; supersonic vs subsonic; Ravi vs Beas) and **swaps between neighbours** (Warangal/Dwarasamudra; zakat/khams; Chishti/Suhrawardi; Beijing/Tashkent). Mix: **15 Easy / 25 Moderate / 10 Hard** - more than three Easy items dropped on Saturday means re-read that chapter the same evening.

## Questions


### Polity - Other Constitutional Dimensions: Official Language, Public Services, Rights & Liabilities of Government, Special Provisions, Co-operative Societies (Laxmikanth)

**Q1.** Which of the following languages were added to the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution by the Constitution (Ninety-second Amendment) Act, 2003?
1. Bodo
2. Konkani
3. Maithili
4. Santhali
5. Dogri
6. Nepali
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

- (a) 1, 3, 4 and 5 only
- (b) 1, 2, 4 and 6 only
- (c) 2, 3, 5 and 6 only
- (d) 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 only

**Q2.** With reference to Article 343 of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the Union shall be Hindi in Devanagari script.
2. The form of numerals to be used for the official purposes of the Union shall be the Devanagari form of numerals.
3. Parliament may by law provide for the continued use of English for official purposes of the Union even after fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

- (a) 1 only
- (b) 1 and 3 only
- (c) 2 and 3 only
- (d) 1, 2 and 3

**Q3.** Consider the following statements regarding Article 344 of the Constitution:
1. It required the President to constitute a Commission at the expiration of five years, and again at the expiration of ten years, from the commencement of the Constitution.
2. It provides for a Committee of thirty members of Parliament - twenty from the Lok Sabha and ten from the Rajya Sabha.
3. The members of that Committee are nominated by the Speaker and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha respectively.
4. The first Official Language Commission was headed by B.G. Kher.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

- (a) 1, 2 and 4 only
- (b) 1 and 2 only
- (c) 2, 3 and 4 only
- (d) 1, 2, 3 and 4

**Q4.** Consider the following statements:
1. Until Parliament by law otherwise provides, all proceedings in the Supreme Court and in every High Court shall be in the English language.
2. The Governor of a State may, with the previous consent of the President, authorise the use of Hindi or the official language of the State in proceedings in the High Court of that State.
3. Such an authorisation under Article 348(2) also extends to judgments, decrees and orders passed by that High Court.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

- (a) 1 only
- (b) 2 and 3 only
- (c) 1 and 2 only
- (d) 1, 2 and 3

**Q5.** Consider the following statements:
1. Article 350A directs every State to endeavour to provide facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.
2. The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B is appointed by the President.
3. The status of a 'classical language' is conferred under a provision of the Eighth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

- (a) 1 and 2 only
- (b) 2 only
- (c) 1 and 3 only
- (d) 1, 2 and 3

**Q6.** Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 310, members of the defence services, the civil services of the Union and the all-India services hold office during the pleasure of the President.
2. The safeguards of Article 311 are equally available to members of the defence services.
3. Under Article 311(1), a civil servant cannot be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which he was appointed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

- (a) 1 and 2 only
- (b) 2 and 3 only
- (c) 1 and 3 only
- (d) 1, 2 and 3

**Q7.** The inquiry ordinarily required under Article 311(2) before dismissal, removal or reduction in rank of a civil servant need NOT be held in which of the following situations?
1. The penalty is imposed on the ground of conduct which has led to his conviction on a criminal charge.
2. The disciplinary authority is satisfied, for reasons to be recorded in writing, that it is not reasonably practicable to hold the inquiry.
3. The President or the Governor is satisfied that in the interest of the security of the State it is not expedient to hold the inquiry.
4. The civil servant is on probation at the time of the action.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

- (a) 1 and 2 only
- (b) 2, 3 and 4 only
- (c) 1, 2, 3 and 4
- (d) 1, 2 and 3 only

**Q8.** With reference to Article 312 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. A new all-India service can be created by Parliament if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. The IAS and the IPS are deemed to be services created by Parliament under this Article.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

- (a) 1 and 2 only
- (b) 2, 3 and 4 only
- (c) 1, 3 and 4 only
- (d) 1, 2 and 3 only

**Q9.** Consider the following statements:

## Answer key with explanations

**Q1. (a) 1, 3, 4 and 5 only** *[Moderate - Eighth Schedule - languages added by the 92nd Amendment, 2003]*

The 92nd Amendment (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali, taking the Schedule from 18 to 22 languages. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali came earlier through the 71st Amendment (1992); Sindhi through the 21st (1967). Learn the three batches as 1 + 3 + 4.

**Q2. (b) 1 and 3 only** *[Easy - Article 343 - official language of the Union, numerals, 15-year English window]*

Statement 2 is the trap: Article 343(1) prescribes the international form of Indian numerals, not Devanagari numerals. Article 343(3) let Parliament extend English beyond 15 years; the Official Languages Act, 1963 (amended 1967) did so, and English now continues indefinitely alongside Hindi.

**Q3. (a) 1, 2 and 4 only** *[Hard - Article 344 - Official Language Commission and Committee of Parliament]*

Statement 3 is wrong: under Article 344(4) the Committee's members are elected by the members of each House by proportional representation through the single transferable vote - not nominated. The first Commission (1955) was chaired by B.G. Kher, and a parliamentary committee then examined its report.

**Q4. (c) 1 and 2 only** *[Moderate - Article 348 - language of the Supreme Court, High Courts and Bills; 348(2)]*

Article 348(1) keeps English for Supreme Court and High Court proceedings (and for authoritative texts of Bills and Acts) until Parliament provides otherwise. Article 348(2) lets the Governor, with the President's previous consent, authorise Hindi or the State language in High Court proceedings - but expressly excludes judgments, decrees and orders. So 3 is wrong.

**Q5. (a) 1 and 2 only** *[Moderate - Articles 350A and 350B; classical language status]*

Articles 350A and 350B were both inserted by the 7th Amendment (1956); the Special Officer is appointed by the President and reports to him. Classical-language status is an executive categorisation by the Union Government (Ministry of Culture), not a constitutional one - the Constitution has no 'classical language' provision. There are 11 such languages after the October 2024 additions.

**Q6. (c) 1 and 3 only** *[Moderate - Articles 310 and 311 - doctrine of pleasure and its safeguards]*

Article 310 codifies the English doctrine of pleasure and covers defence personnel too. Article 311, however, protects only persons who are members of a civil service of the Union or a State, an all-India service, or who hold a civil post - defence personnel are outside it. So the pleasure is wider than the protection; statement 2 is wrong.

**Q7. (d) 1, 2 and 3 only** *[Hard - Article 311(2) - the three exceptions to the inquiry requirement]*

The second proviso to Article 311(2) lists exactly three exceptions: criminal conviction, impracticability (reasons recorded in writing), and security of the State (satisfaction of the President or Governor). Probation is not a constitutional exception - a probationer's termination is governed by service rules and case law, not by the proviso.

**Q8. (d) 1, 2 and 3 only** *[Moderate - Article 312 - creation of all-India services]*

Statements 1-3 are correct: Article 312(1) needs the Rajya Sabha resolution (2/3 present and voting) - the Council of States' federal consent; Article 312(2) deems the IAS and IPS to be Parliament-created; the Indian Forest Service followed in 1966. Statement 4 is wrong: all-India services are under joint Union-State control, with ultimate control (recruitment, cadre, major penalties) resting with the Centre.

**Q9. (b) 1 and 3 only** *[Easy - Articles 299 and 300 - Government contracts and suits]*

Article 299(1) requires Union contracts to be expressed as made by the President; Article 299(2) expressly says neither the President nor the person executing the contract is personally liable. Article 300 lets the Government of India sue and be sued as 'the Union of India' (and a State by its name). Statement 2 is the inversion.

**Q10. (a) Kasturi Lal Ralia Ram Jain v. State of Uttar Pradesh** *[Hard - Sovereign immunity - Kasturi Lal (1965)]*

Kasturi Lal (1965) - gold seized by police and misappropriated - applied the sovereign/non-sovereign distinction and denied compensation. Vidyawati (1962) held the State liable for a government jeep accident (non-sovereign). Nagendra Rao (1994) diluted the sovereign-immunity defence. Rudul Sah (1983) is the landmark on compensation for illegal detention under Article 32.

**Q11. (c) 1 and 2 only** *[Moderate - Article 334 and the 104th Amendment, 2019]*

The 104th Amendment amended Article 334 to extend SC/ST seat reservation to 80 years from commencement (25 January 2030) and let the Anglo-Indian nomination under Articles 331 and 333 lapse from January 2020. Job reservation under Article 16(4)/335 carries no time limit, so there was nothing to extend - statement 3 is wrong.

**Q12. (d) 1, 2 and 3** *[Moderate - Backward classes - Articles 338B, 340, 342A; 102nd and 105th Amendments]*

All three are correct. The 102nd Amendment inserted Articles 338B and 342A; after the Maratha-reservation judgment read 342A as centralising SEBC identification, the 105th Amendment (2021) restored the States' power to maintain their own lists. Article 340 is the basis of both the Kaka Kalelkar (1953) and Mandal (1979) Commissions.

**Q13. (b) 1, 2 and 3 only** *[Moderate - 97th Amendment, 2011 - what it changed]*

The 97th Amendment touched three places: Article 19(1)(c) (co-operatives joined associations and unions), Article 43B (DPSP) and Part IXB (Articles 243ZH-243ZT). It did not touch the Seventh Schedule - co-operative societies remain Entry 32 of the State List, which is exactly why ratification became the issue in Rajendra N. Shah.

**Q14. (c) 1 and 3 only** *[Hard - Union of India v. Rajendra N. Shah (2021) - Part IXB]*

The majority held that Part IXB significantly affected State List Entry 32 and so needed ratification under the proviso to Article 368(2), which it never received. It did not strike the Part wholesale: provisions dealing with multi-State co-operative societies (a Union subject) were held severable and valid. Statement 2 is the overreach trap.

**Q15. (c) 1, 2 and 3 only** *[Easy - Human Development Index - dimensions]*

HDI = geometric mean of three dimension indices: life expectancy at birth; mean and expected years of schooling; GNI per capita (PPP). Inequality is not in the HDI itself - it is captured by the separate Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI), and gender gaps by the GDI/GII.

**Q16. (a) 1 and 2 only** *[Moderate - National Multidimensional Poverty Index - structure and publishers]*

India's national MPI keeps the global MPI's three equally weighted dimensions and its ten indicators, and adds two - maternal health and bank account - for twelve. The global MPI is produced by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) with UNDP, not the World Bank (which publishes the monetary poverty lines such as USD 3.00/day PPP).

**Q17. (d) 1, 2 and 3** *[Hard - Poverty lines - Tendulkar vs Rangarajan]*

All correct. Tendulkar (2009) dropped the calorie anchor, used a single all-India poverty line basket (the urban basket) for both rural and urban India, and valued health and education spending - giving 21.9% poverty for 2011-12. Rangarajan (2014) went back to a calorie-protein-fat norm plus non-food needs and raised the lines, giving 29.5% for the same year.

**Q18. (a) 1 and 2 only** *[Easy - Gross vs Net Enrolment Ratio]*

GER divides all enrolment at a level, of any age, by the official-age population - so over-age and under-age pupils can push it above 100. NER counts only official-age pupils in the numerator, so it cannot exceed 100; the GER-NER gap is itself a measure of over/under-age enrolment. Statement 3 is wrong.

**Q19. (c) 1 and 3 only** *[Moderate - Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - cover and eligibility]*

PM-JAY (September 2018) is a hospitalisation scheme: Rs 5 lakh per family per year, cashless, for secondary and tertiary care. Primary care is the job of the other pillar of Ayushman Bharat - the Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (health and wellness centres) - so statement 2 is wrong. The October 2024 expansion covers all persons 70+ regardless of income.

**Q20. (b) the last 7 days preceding the survey** *[Easy - PLFS - usual status vs current weekly status]*

PLFS (NSO, since 2017-18) uses three yardsticks: Usual Status (reference period 365 days, principal + subsidiary), Current Weekly Status (7 days) and Current Daily Status (each day of the reference week, in half-day units). CWS unemployment is higher than usual-status unemployment because it catches short spells.

**Q21. (b) 1 and 2 only** *[Easy - Gini coefficient and the Lorenz curve]*

The Gini coefficient is the area between the 45-degree line of equality and the Lorenz curve, divided by the whole area under the line of equality. 0 = perfect equality; 1 = one household holds all income. So statement 3 inverts the scale.

**Q22. (b) Muhammad bin Qasim** *[Easy - Arab conquest of Sindh, 712]*

Muhammad bin Qasim, sent under the Umayyad Caliphate by the governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf, defeated Raja Dahir and took Sindh and Multan. Mahmud's raids came three centuries later (c. 1000-1027); Ghori's campaigns laid the Sultanate's foundation in the 1190s.

**Q23. (d) 1, 2 and 3** *[Easy - Battles of Tarain and Chandawar]*

All three are correct. Tarain I (1191) was Ghori's defeat; Tarain II (1192) opened the Ganga plain; Chandawar (1194) removed the Gahadavalas. Aibak, Ghori's slave-general, was left in charge of the Indian conquests and became Sultan in 1206.

**Q24. (a) 1 and 2 only** *[Easy - Al-Biruni and Kitab-ul-Hind]*

Al-Biruni (from Khwarizm) accompanied Mahmud, learnt Sanskrit and wrote Kitab-ul-Hind in Arabic - a systematic account of Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and society. The court poet of the Khaljis (and later rulers) was Amir Khusrau, not Al-Biruni.

**Q25. (d) Construction of the Alai Darwaza** *[Easy - Iltutmish - coinage, investiture, the Forty]*

Iltutmish (1211-36) is the real consolidator: silver tanka and copper jital, the iqta system, the Forty, and investiture from the Abbasid Caliph (1229). He also completed the Qutb Minar begun by Aibak. The Alai Darwaza (1311), the gateway to the Quwwat-ul-Islam complex, was built by Alauddin Khalji.

**Q26. (c) 1, 2 and 3 only** *[Moderate - Balban - theory of kingship]*

Balban (1266-87) raised the Sultan's prestige through Persian court ritual (sijda - prostration; paibos - kissing the feet), the doctrine of the Sultan as God's shadow, and by destroying the Forty of which he had himself been a member. Token currency belongs to Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1329-30).

**Q27. (b) 1, 2 and 3 only** *[Hard - Alauddin Khalji - market control and military reforms]*

Statement 4 is the trap: Alauddin raised the demand to half (50%) of the produce, assessed by measurement (masahat). The market regime - price control through the Shahna-i-Mandi and the Diwan-i-Riyasat, with a spy network - served a large standing army paid in cash, which is why dagh and huliya belong to the same package.

**Q28. (b) Only two** *[Moderate - Malik Kafur's Deccan campaigns - capitals and dynasties]*

Only 1 and 4 are correct. Warangal was the Kakatiya capital (Prataparudra) and Dwarasamudra the Hoysala capital (Ballala III) - the two are swapped. Kafur's campaigns (1307-11) ran Devagiri -> Warangal -> Dwarasamudra -> Madurai, extracting tribute rather than annexing.

**Q29. (d) All four** *[Hard - Muhammad bin Tughlaq - experiments]*

All four are correct. The Daulatabad transfer (1327), token currency (1329-30), the Doab tax increase, and the agricultural department Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi are the four 'experiments'. Ibn Battuta arrived in 1333, was appointed qazi of Delhi, and later wrote the Rihla.

**Q30. (a) 1, 2 and 3 only** *[Moderate - Firoz Shah Tughlaq - departments and public works]*

Firoz (1351-88) set up the Diwan-i-Khairat and the Diwan-i-Bandagan, dug canals, levied the irrigation tax haq-i-sharb, and moved the Topra and Meerut Ashokan pillars to Delhi. Far from abolishing jizya, he extended it to Brahmins, who had earlier been exempt. Jizya was abolished by Akbar (1564).

**Q31. (c) 4-2-1-3** *[Moderate - Sultanate chronology]*

Kafur reaches Madurai in 1311 (Khalji); the capital shifts to Daulatabad in 1327 (Muhammad bin Tughlaq); Timur sacks Delhi in 1398 (under Nasiruddin Mahmud Tughlaq); Sikandar Lodi founds Agra in 1504. Khalji -> Tughlaq -> Timur -> Lodi.

**Q32. (c) Only three** *[Moderate - Sultanate revenue terms]*

Pair 3 is wrong: zakat is the religious tax on the property of well-off Muslims; the one-fifth share of war booty is khams (under the rule the state took one-fifth and the soldiers four-fifths; Alauddin is said to have reversed the proportion). Haq-i-sharb, the water tax on canal-irrigated land, is associated with Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

**Q33. (b) 1 and 2 only** *[Moderate - Sufi silsilas and their centres]*

Bahauddin Zakariya founded the Suhrawardi order at Multan - and, unlike the Chishtis, the Suhrawardis accepted state patronage and grants. Moinuddin (Ajmer) and Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi; Amir Khusrau was his disciple) are the Chishti pillars.

**Q34. (b) 1, 2 and 3 only** *[Easy - Export control regimes - India's memberships]*

India joined the MTCR (2016), the Wassenaar Arrangement (2017, conventional arms and dual-use goods) and the Australia Group (2018, chemical and biological). Its NSG membership bid remains blocked (it has only the 2008 NSG waiver).

**Q35. (b) 1, 2 and 4 only** *[Hard - Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor, Kalpakkam]*

A fast reactor uses no moderator - it needs fast neutrons to convert fertile U-238 in the blanket into fissile Pu-239, which is why it can breed more fuel than it consumes; heavy water is the moderator of first-stage PHWRs. The 500 MWe PFBR, built by BHAVINI with MOX fuel and liquid-sodium cooling, attained first criticality on 6 April 2026 (DAE). It is the second-stage gateway to thorium use.

**Q36. (a) 1 and 2 only** *[Moderate - Hypersonic weapons - HGV, scramjet]*

A scramjet (supersonic-combustion ramjet) is air-breathing: it takes oxygen from the atmosphere, which is precisely what powers hypersonic cruise missiles. A glide vehicle (HGV) is unpowered after boost; its low, manoeuvring flight path is what defeats ballistic-missile defences.

**Q37. (c) 1, 2 and 3 only** *[Moderate - ITER - fusion project]*

ITER (India joined in 2005; the other members are the EU, China, Japan, Korea, Russia and the US) is an experimental tokamak meant to prove net fusion power at scale using D-T fusion. It will not sell power to any grid - demonstration reactors are meant to follow it.

**Q38. (d) 1, 2 and 3** *[Moderate - INSTC and the Ashgabat Agreement]*

All three are correct. The INSTC (St Petersburg, 2000) runs Mumbai -> Bandar Abbas -> Caspian -> Astrakhan/Moscow. The Ashgabat Agreement (2011; Iran, Oman, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, later Kazakhstan, Pakistan and India) is a multimodal Central Asia-Gulf corridor; India joined on 3 February 2018, complementing INSTC and Chabahar.

**Q39. (b) on the Gulf of Oman, outside the Strait of Hormuz** *[Moderate - Chabahar - location]*

Chabahar is in Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan province on the Gulf of Oman - outside Hormuz, ~170 km west of Pakistan's Gwadar. Bandar Abbas sits on the Strait of Hormuz. India's IPGL runs the Shahid Beheshti terminal (10-year contract signed May 2024).

**Q40. (b) 1 and 3 only** *[Moderate - India-Russia defence cooperation - BrahMos, AK-203]*

BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile (about Mach 2.8) - India's subsonic cruise missile programme is Nirbhay. The AK-203 JV at Korwa (Amethi, UP) is an Indo-Russian joint venture involving the OFB successor companies and Rosoboronexport/Kalashnikov.

**Q41. (c) Tamil Nadu** *[Easy - Kudankulam - Russian nuclear cooperation]*

Kudankulam (Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu) uses Russian-designed VVER-1000 pressurised light-water reactors, built by NPCIL with Rosatom. It is the flagship of India-Russia civil nuclear cooperation.

**Q42. (d) 3, 4 and 5 only** *[Hard - Central Asia - states bordering Afghanistan]*

Tajikistan (the longest border, along the Amu Darya/Panj), Uzbekistan (the shortest, at Termez) and Turkmenistan border Afghanistan. Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan do not. The Ayni airbase, long associated with Indian assistance, is in Tajikistan.

**Q43. (a) 1 and 2 only** *[Moderate - Shanghai Cooperation Organisation - structure]*

India and Pakistan joined at the Astana summit (June 2017). SCO has two permanent bodies: the Secretariat in Beijing and RATS in Tashkent. Statement 3 is wrong.

**Q44. (d) 1, 2 and 3** *[Hard - Target-area and hill-area programmes (NCERT-12 Ch 9)]*

All three are straight from NCERT-12 Ch 9. The Hill Area programmes (Fifth Plan) initially covered 15 districts - the hill districts of present Uttarakhand, Mikir Hills and North Cachar (Assam), Darjeeling and the Nilgiris. The DPAP (Fourth Plan) was meant to provide employment and create productive assets in drought-prone areas; the Desert Development Programme is its companion.

**Q45. (a) 1 and 2 only** *[Moderate - Bharmaur tribal region - case study]*

Bharmaur (Bharmaur and Holi tehsils, Chamba) has been a notified tribal area since 1975 and was developed under the Integrated Tribal Development Project from the Fifth Plan. It is drained by the Ravi and its tributaries, the Budhil and the Tundahen - not the Beas.

**Q46. (b) 1, 2 and 3 only** *[Moderate - Indira Gandhi Canal - command area]*

Harike barrage (Satluj-Beas confluence) is the source; the canal runs roughly 40 km inside the border. Stage-I covers Ganganagar, Hanumangarh and northern Bikaner; Stage-II covers Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Barmer, Jodhpur, Nagaur and Churu. Intensive irrigation has brought waterlogging and salinity, the core sustainability critique in NCERT.

**Q47. (a) Silchar and Porbandar** *[Easy - North-South and East-West corridors]*

The North-South Corridor links Srinagar and Kanyakumari; the East-West Corridor links Silchar (Assam) and Porbandar (Gujarat); the two intersect at Jhansi. The Golden Quadrilateral links Delhi-Mumbai-Chennai-Kolkata.

**Q48. (d) All three** *[Easy - National Waterways 1-3]*

All three are correct. NW-1 (about 1,620 km) is the longest; NW-2 about 891 km; NW-3 about 205 km in Kerala (with the Champakara and Udyogamandal canals). The National Waterways Act, 2016 raised the total to 111.

**Q49. (b) 1 and 3 only** *[Moderate - Oil and gas pipelines]*

Salaya-Mathura is a crude-oil pipeline from the Gujarat coast (Salaya, Gulf of Kutch) to the Mathura refinery, with branches to Panipat - statement 2 is wrong. HBJ (GAIL) is the country's first cross-state gas trunk line; the Naharkatia-Nunmati-Barauni line (later extended to Kanpur) is the NCERT's 'first' crude pipeline.

**Q50. (a) 1 and 2 only** *[Easy - Konkan Railway]*

NCERT-12 Ch 10: the Konkan Railway (1998) connects Roha (Maharashtra) to Mangaluru (Karnataka), about 760 km, crossing some 146 rivers and over 2,000 bridges. It runs through three States - Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka - not four.

## Revision checklist

- [ ] Eighth Schedule batches: 21st (1967) Sindhi; 71st (1992) Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali; 92nd (2003) Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali - 22 total.
- [ ] Art 343: Hindi in Devanagari + **international** form of numerals; English window 15 years -> OLA 1963 (am. 1967) indefinite.
- [ ] Art 344 Committee: 30 MPs (20 LS + 10 RS), **elected** by PR-STV; first Commission B.G. Kher (1955).
- [ ] Art 348(2): Governor + President's prior consent -> Hindi/State language in HC proceedings, **not** judgments, decrees, orders.
- [ ] Arts 350A/350B (7th Amdt 1956); classical-language status is executive, 11 languages.
- [ ] Art 310 covers defence; Art 311 does not. The three 311(2) exceptions: conviction, impracticability (reasons in writing), security of the State.
- [ ] Art 312: RS resolution, 2/3 present and voting; IAS/IPS deemed; Indian Forest Service 1966.
- [ ] Arts 299/300: contracts in the President's name, no personal liability; 'Union of India' sues and is sued. Kasturi Lal (1965) vs Vidyawati (1962) vs Nagendra Rao (1994).
- [ ] 104th Amdt: SC/ST seats to Jan 2030; Anglo-Indian nomination ended. 102nd (338B, 342A) and 105th (States' SEBC lists).
- [ ] 97th Amdt: 19(1)(c) + 43B + Part IXB; *Rajendra N. Shah* (2021) - struck for State co-ops, saved for multi-State co-ops.
- [ ] HDI (3 dimensions, geometric mean) vs national MPI (3 dimensions, 12 indicators; global MPI by OPHI-UNDP); Tendulkar 21.9% vs Rangarajan 29.5% (2011-12).
- [ ] PLFS: Usual Status 365 days, CWS 7 days, CDS each day of the week; GER can exceed 100, NER cannot.
- [ ] Sultanate spine: 712 Qasim -> 1191/92 Tarain -> 1194 Chandawar -> 1206 Mamluks -> 1229 investiture -> 1290 Khaljis -> 1311 Madurai -> 1320 Tughlaqs -> 1327 Daulatabad -> 1398 Timur -> 1504 Agra -> 1526 Panipat.
- [ ] Kafur's capitals: Devagiri-Yadava, Warangal-Kakatiya, Dwarasamudra-Hoysala, Madurai-Pandya. Taxes: kharaj, jizya, zakat, khams, haq-i-sharb.
- [ ] Regimes: MTCR 2016, Wassenaar 2017, Australia Group 2018, not NSG. PFBR: sodium, MOX, no moderator, criticality 6 Apr 2026.
- [ ] Eurasia map: INSTC (2000), Ashgabat (India 2018), Chabahar on the Gulf of Oman; Afghanistan's Central Asian neighbours = Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan; SCO Secretariat Beijing, RATS Tashkent.
- [ ] Geography: HADP 5th Plan, DPAP 4th Plan, 600 m criterion; Bharmaur = Chamba/Gaddi/Ravi; IGNP from Harike; EW corridor Silchar-Porbandar; NW 1/2/3; Salaya-Mathura is crude; Konkan 1998, Roha-Mangaluru, 3 States.
